npcs.name: Sigrun Tovesdottir
npcs.idle: Hallvard. You haven't seen a big, slow, kind man called Hallvard? No. Of course not.

npcs.name: Old Grima
npcs.idle: The hidden folk are older than the jarls. Older than the gods, some say. Only fools say it loudly.

npcs.name: Bjarki Houndmaster
npcs.idle: A good hound is worth three huscarls. Don't tell the huscarls.

npcs.name: Huscarl-Captain Ragnhild
npcs.idle: Mularn sleeps sound because somebody doesn't. Tonight that's me.

npcs.name: Seeress Ingrith
npcs.idle: The well at Haggerfel shows me things. Lately it shows me snow, and a red eye in the dark.

npcs.name: Warden Thorvald
npcs.idle: Fort Veldon watches the north road. Lately the north road watches back.

npcs.name: Eydis the Go-Between
npcs.idle: My grandmother married one of the hidden folk. Don't laugh. It's why they talk to me.

quests.title: The Huldra's Bargain
quests.offer:
Hallvard and I are to be wed at midsummer. Or we were. He went into the western woods to cut timber for our house, and came back once, a week ago - singing, smelling of pine and cream - and went straight back out again.

Old [Grima] says it's a huldra. One of the hidden folk. Will you [find Hallvard]? Before midsummer, if you can.

topics.Grima: Old Grima, by the well. She knows every story worth knowing.

quests.summary: Sigrun's betrothed went into the western woods to cut timber and came back singing - then went back to the hidden folk.

steps.goal: Ask Old Grima about the hidden folk
steps.say: A huldra. Fair as morning from the front, and a cow's [tail] behind - that's how you know. She'll have a camp in the west, with her kin. If a huldra weds a man under the gods, she loses the tail and becomes a woman. They want that very much. Some of them want it more than they want the man.

steps.text: Somewhere ahead, someone is singing - a man, badly, and a woman, beautifully.
The hidden folk fade back into the trees, watching. They don't seem to want to fight. They seem to want you to leave.

clue.name: a woodsman's axe, left in a stump

steps.text: Hallvard's axe, its edge rusting. He hasn't cut a tree in a week. Beyond the tents, in the firelight, a big man sits with a beautiful woman's head on his shoulder.

steps.say:
Sigrun sent you? Oh. Oh, Sigrun.

This is Ylva. Look at her. She says she'll lose her tail if we wed at the temple, and be a woman, and grow old with me. She cried when she said it. Nobody's ever cried over me. I don't know what to [do].

I promised Sigrun. I did. But I didn't know there was this. Tell me.

Should I [wed Ylva]? Or should you [break the glamour] and drag me home by the beard? Ylva's father won't let me go easy, if you do.

options.say: ...Yes. Yes. Tell Sigrun I'm sorry. Tell her she'll find someone who deserves her. I mean that.
Then do it quick, before I change my mind - her father's coming. Gods, look at the size of him.

steps.text: The old hill-man falls. Ylva is gone - only a scent of pine. Hallvard blinks like a man waking up.

stages.name: Old Grumme of the Hidden Folk
stages.announce: An old huldu man rises from the fire, horns and all. 'He's promised to my girl. You'll not take him.'

boss.name: Old Grumme of the Hidden Folk

stages.success: Old Grumme of the Hidden Folk falls.

steps.say:
He's home. He looks like a man who woke up from a lovely dream into a cold morning, and he says sorry every hour.

I'll take him. Sorry and all. Midsummer's still a month off.

He's marrying her. A huldra. At the temple, so she can be a woman.

Then I hope she's a better one than me, because I'm going to hate her for the rest of my life. ...No. That's not fair. Take this. It was meant for the wedding.

home.text: Take this - for bringing him home.

wed.text: It was meant for the wedding.

quests.title: The Houndmaster's Law
quests.offer:
My hounds went mad in a night. Foaming, howling, gone west into the moor. Gormr led them - my son's dog. My son's dead two winters, and Gormr's all of him I've got.

Gormr bit a child before he ran. The jarl's law says a dog that bites a child is killed. I know the law. Will you [find my hounds] and find out what did this? I'll deal with the law after.
quests.summary: Bjarki Houndmaster's hounds went mad and ran west, led by his dead son's dog.

steps.text: Hounds - Bjarki's hounds - roam the heather, foaming at the mouth, savage and lost.

steps.goal: Put down the worst of the rabid hounds
steps.text: Every one wears Bjarki's brass tag. Every one had drunk from the same spring - their muzzles are stained with its grey water.
Bone fetishes, strung on sinew and sunk in the spring - vendo work. The water is grey with curse. Tracks of clawed feet lead north, to the vendo camps.

steps.goal: Kill the vendo shaman who cursed the spring
steps.text: The bone-singer's chant chokes off. Far to the south, all at once, the howling stops.

stages.name: Bone-Singer Grakka
stages.announce: A vendo in a mask of skulls rises out of a pile of bones, rattling and singing. 'Dog-man's dogs! Dog-man's dogs, mad and mine!'

steps.say:
The fever's broken. Look at them - lying in the grass like puppies, sorry for themselves. And Gormr. Gormr's here.

He's himself again. But he bit the Sveinsson girl. The jarl's law is the law: you saw it, so you must say. Do I [keep the law]? Or do we [say nothing], and Gormr was never found?

options.say: ...Yes. I'll do it myself. He's my son's dog. He'll not die by a stranger's hand. Go back to Fort Veldon. I'll follow.
Never found. Lost on the moor. Aye. Aye. Gods forgive us both. Come on, boy. Come on, Gormr.

steps.say:
It's done. He didn't fight. He licked my hand.

The jarl thanked me for my loyalty. I nearly hit him. Here. Gormr's collar. I can't keep it in the house.

Gormr was never found, if anyone asks. Lost on the moor.

He's asleep under my bed. Snoring. Here - take something. You've given me back more than a dog.

quests.title: The Pranksters
quests.offer:
Hobgoblins. Little grey things with bells on. They've cut the ropes off the well, painted the shrine, and put a goat on the jarl's roof. Twice.

It's not war. It's worse - it's embarrassing. Will you [chase them off]?
quests.summary: Hobgoblin pranksters are making fools of Mularn.

steps.goal: Chase off the hobgoblin pranksters about 210 m north-west of Huscarl-Captain Ragnhild

steps.say: Good. The goat's still on the roof. One thing at a time.

quests.title: The Jarl's Ale
quests.offer:
The little water goblins in the meadow ponds have stolen a keg of the jarl's ale. They can't even drink it - it makes them sick. They do it for spite.

Will you [get the keg back]?
quests.summary: Little water goblins stole a keg of the jarl's ale.

steps.goal: Drive off the little water goblins about 310 m north-west of Huscarl-Captain Ragnhild

clue.name: a muddy keg in the reeds

steps.text: The keg - half empty, and three water goblins asleep in the reeds beside it, looking very sorry for themselves.

steps.say: Half empty. The jarl will notice. I'll tell him you drank it - he'll like you better.

quests.title: In the Cellars
quests.offer:
Vein spiderlings in the meadows south of town, hatching by the hundred. Give it a month and they're in the cellars.

Will you [thin them out]?
quests.summary: Vein spiderlings are hatching in the meadows south of Mularn.

steps.goal: Thin out the vein spiderlings about 270 m north of Huscarl-Captain Ragnhild

steps.say: Fewer. That's all you can ask with spiders - fewer.

quests.title: The Snake-Finders
quests.offer:
The hobgoblin snake-finders bag up mud snakes and let them loose on the Haggerfel road. Carters have stopped coming.

Will you [clear the road]?
quests.summary: Hobgoblin snake-finders loose snakes on the road between Mularn and Haggerfel.

steps.goal: Stop the hobgoblin snake-finders about 460 m north of Huscarl-Captain Ragnhild

steps.say: The carters will be glad. Seeress Ingrith in Haggerfel wants to meet you, by the way - she says she saw you in her well.

quests.title: The Wood-Eaters
quests.offer:
The wood-eaters in the south have eaten the bridge at Jordheim road. The whole bridge. They're eating the fence-posts now.

Will you [push them back]?
quests.summary: Wood-eaters from the hive in the south are eating Mularn's fences and bridges.

steps.goal: Push back the wood-eaters about 320 m west of Huscarl-Captain Ragnhild

steps.say: Back to their hive. Which is growing. Which is a problem for later, and later is getting close.

quests.title: Hive Hunters
quests.offer:
The hive sends hunters now, out as far as the meadows. One took a calf yesterday. Wood-eaters don't eat calves. Something's changed down there.

Will you [hunt the hunters]?
quests.summary: Wood-eater hunters range out of the hive and take Mularn's calves.

steps.goal: Hunt the wood-eater hunters about 370 m north-west of Huscarl-Captain Ragnhild

steps.say: A new king in the hive, then. A hungry one. Bring friends when you go for him.

quests.title: The Hive King
quests.offer:
The new wood-eater king sits in the hive's heart with his royal guard round him. Kill him and the hive goes back to eating trees, not calves.

It's a job for a few of you. Will you [go into the hive]?
quests.summary: A hungry new king rules the wood-eater hive south of Mularn.

steps.goal: Bring down the wood-eater king about 460 m west of Huscarl-Captain Ragnhild

steps.say: The jarl wants to give you something. I talked him down from the goat.

quests.title: Milk in the Night
quests.offer:
The huldu lurkers have been stealing milk from the farms. That isn't new - you leave out a bowl, and they leave you alone. But they're taking the pails now, and the cows.

Something is frightening them. Will you [drive them back]? Gently, if you can.
quests.summary: Huldu lurkers have begun stealing pails and cows from the farms by the western woods.

steps.goal: Drive back the huldu lurkers about 80 m north of Eydis the Go-Between

steps.say: They're frightened. The hidden folk don't frighten easily. Something in the west is moving.

quests.title: The Outcasts
quests.offer:
The huldu outcasts - the ones their own folk turned out - camp near the farms now. They say they're hiding. From what, they won't say.

The farmers want them gone. Will you [move them on]? They'll go further west, at least.
quests.summary: Huldu outcasts, turned out by their own folk, camp near the western farms.

steps.goal: Move on the huldu outcasts about 90 m south-west of Eydis the Go-Between

steps.say: One of them said a word as she went. 'Fimbul.' I hope I heard wrong.

quests.title: The Ring of White Stones
quests.offer:
The hidden folk keep a ring of white stones in the western woods. When they want to speak to us, they leave a letter there - birch-bark. My well says there's one waiting.

The huldu stalkers guard the ring. Will you [fetch the letter]?
quests.summary: The hidden folk have left a birch-bark letter at their ring of white stones in the western woods.

steps.goal: Go to the huldu ring in the western woods
steps.text: White stones in a circle, and in the middle a fresh birch with its bark half peeled. The stalkers watch you from the trees.

steps.goal: Search the ring of white stones

clue.name: birch-bark, rolled and tied with hair

steps.text: The letter is in old runes. Even you can read the last line: 'THE WINTER WALKS. EVEN WE WILL HIDE.'

steps.goal: Bring the letter to Seeress Ingrith
steps.say:
'The winter walks.' Fimbulwinter - the winter that comes before the end. The hidden folk have never written to us about anything bigger than cows.

I need to look in the well. Come back - Warden Thorvald at Fort Veldon has hounds that won't stop howling. Go and see him.

quests.title: Darkness Falls
quests.offer:
Phantom hounds at Darkness Falls, in the west. They always ran there - ghosts of hounds, harmless mostly. Now they hunt. They've killed two shepherds.

Will you [lay them]?
quests.summary: The phantom hounds of Darkness Falls have begun to hunt.

steps.goal: Lay the phantom hounds about 1.0 km south-west of Warden Thorvald

steps.say: They were running from something, not hunting. My own hounds do the same at night now - howl at the north-west and won't stop.

quests.title: Gone Wild
quests.offer:
Somebody's wolfhounds - big ones, good hunting dogs - have gone wild on the ridge west of Haggerfel. Rabid. They had masters once.

I hate this job. Will you [do it for me]?
quests.summary: Rabid wolfhounds that once had masters run wild on the ridge west of Haggerfel.

steps.goal: Put down the rabid wolfhounds about 580 m south-west of Warden Thorvald

steps.say: Thank you. One of them wore a collar from a farm in West Svealand. They came a long way to go mad here.

quests.title: The Frost in the Tracks
quests.offer:
The shepherds by Darkness Falls swear they've seen a wolf as big as a horse, walking at moonrise. I'd laugh, but my hounds aren't laughing.

Go up past the falls and [find its tracks]. Look. Don't fight it alone.
quests.summary: Shepherds by Darkness Falls swear they've seen a wolf as big as a horse.

steps.text: Wind off the falls, and the smell of snow, in summer.

steps.goal: Look for the great wolf's tracks

clue.name: a paw-print the size of a shield

steps.text: Each print is rimed with frost. In the sun. They come down out of the north-west, out of the mountains - from where the winter doesn't end.

steps.say:
Frost that won't melt. That's Raumarik frost. Gods.

The Moon-Howler, the shepherds call it. If it comes down to the falls again, the whole vale will need to go out against it.

quests.title: The Bone-Collectors
quests.offer:
The vendo - the wild men of the north caves - have started digging up the old barrows and carrying the bones home. They never did that before.

Will you [stop the digging]?
quests.summary: The vendo of the northern caves are digging up the old barrows.

steps.goal: Stop the vendo bone-collectors about 760 m north-west of Seeress Ingrith

steps.say: They were carrying the bones TO someone. The well shows me a man in a red-scaled cloak, at the cave mouth, preaching.

quests.title: The Red Eye
quests.offer:
The vendo shamans have painted red eyes on their fetishes - a dragon's eye. Their old spirits are being pushed aside.

Will you [break the shamans]? Bring me a fetish if you can.
quests.summary: The vendo shamans have painted a dragon's red eye on their fetishes.

steps.goal: Break the vendo shamans about 710 m north-west of Seeress Ingrith

steps.say: A red eye. Somebody is teaching the vendo to worship a dragon. There is only one dragon in Midgard who wants worshippers.

quests.title: The Dragon-Preacher
quests.offer:
Ingrith's well was right. There's a preacher at the Vendo Caverns - red-scaled cloak, voice like honey - telling the vendo that the gods are finished and a mother-dragon will make them kings.

He has vendo round him. Bring friends, and [silence him].
quests.summary: A drakulv dragon-preacher at the mouth of the Vendo Caverns tells the vendo the gods are finished.

steps.goal: Search the cave mouth for the preacher's tracts

clue.name: red vellum nailed to a post

steps.text: 'THE AESIR ARE OLD. THE WINTER COMES FOR THEM. ONLY THE MOTHER'S FIRE WILL KEEP YOU WARM.' Below it, a dragon's eye.
The preacher falls, still smiling. 'She will come for the Vale. She comes for everything.'

stages.name: Hrafnkel Dragon-Tongue
stages.announce: A man in a cloak of red scales steps out of the cave: 'Come to hear the good news? Midgard is dying. Gjalpinulva will hatch the next one.'

steps.say:
Gjalpinulva. The dragon of Malmohus. So the south has started talking, while the north starts howling.

He had a letter on him. Take it to Ingrith.

quests.title: Two Signs
quests.offer:
Thorvald sent you with the preacher's letter? Let me read it. ... It names Malmohus, and the svartalf traders of Gotar who carry the dragon's word north. And it laughs at us: 'the wolf-winter will finish the Aesir, and the mother will warm what's left.'

Two signs, one letter. Will you [read it with me]? Then we'll decide where it goes.
quests.summary: A drakulv preacher's letter names Malmohus, Gotar's svartalf traders and the wolf-winter.

steps.goal: Decide what to do with the letter
steps.say: To [Jordheim], and the King's huscarls march sooner. Or to [the well], and the volur learn what the dragon knows of the winter.

options.say: Then ride. The King should know what's coming from both ends.
Then sit with me while I read. It'll be a long night.
